section.book: Bittinger, Beecher, Ellenbogen & Penna, College Algebra: Graphs and Models, 7e
section.title: Analyzing Graphs of Quadratic Functions

title: Maximum value of a quadratic function
sources: OpenStax College Algebra 2e §5.1 pp. 395-399 (CC BY 4.0): explanations only, no problems copied
process_card: Finding the maximum or minimum value

problem.prompt: Does f(x) = {tex:fe} have a maximum or a minimum value? Find that value.

steps.name: decide maximum or minimum from the sign of a
give the y-coordinate of the vertex

answer.say: The maximum value is {k}, when x = {h}.

mistakes.name: gave the x-coordinate
mistakes.message: The maximum VALUE is the y-coordinate of the vertex; x = h only says where it happens.

hints.why: The highest or lowest point is the vertex.

hints.step: decide maximum or minimum from the sign of a
hints.hint: a < 0 opens down (maximum); a > 0 opens up (minimum).
hints.why: The vertex is the top of a parabola that opens down and the bottom of one that opens up.

hints.step: give the y-coordinate of the vertex
hints.hint: The value is k, not h.
hints.why: A maximum or minimum value is an output (y).
